factors.name: Topic Consistency
factors.value: 0/2 title keywords align with content topics

recommendations.recommendation: Attribute claims to specific sources or experts. Phrases like "according to" help AI engines trace information.
steps: Identify factual claims that currently have no source
Prepend 'According to [Source]' or 'Per [Organization]' before each claim
Link the source name to its original URL so AI engines can follow the reference
Add a citation marker (e.g., [1]) for formal references tied to a sources section
recommendations.codeExample:
72% of AI-cited content uses question-framed headings.

According to Princeton's GEO research, 72% of AI-cited content uses question-framed headings.

recommendations.recommendation: Add visible author information with a byline to establish content credibility and enable AI attribution.
steps: Add a visible byline near the top of the article (after the H1)
Link the author name to an about/bio page using rel="author"
Add author information to your JSON-LD schema (see code example)
recommendations.codeExample:
By Author Name

"author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "Author Name", "url": "https://yoursite.com/about/author-name" }

recommendations.recommendation: Use formal citation patterns (e.g., [1], "according to") when referencing sources.
steps: Add in-text citation markers like [1] or (Author, Year) after specific claims
Include a 'References' or 'Sources' section at the bottom of the page
Use <cite> elements around titles of books, articles, or research papers
Link each citation marker to its corresponding reference entry
recommendations.codeExample:
AI engines prioritize structured content by a factor of 3x [1].

As described in Generative Engine Optimization, answer density is key.

References

  1. Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) - Aggarwal et al., Princeton University, 2023

recommendations.recommendation: Link to About and Contact pages to establish credibility and enable source verification.
steps: Add links to your About and Contact pages in the site navigation
Include them in the footer of every page
Ensure the links are reachable via plain anchor tags, not JavaScript-only interactions
recommendations.codeExample:
About Us Contact
"contactPoint": { "@type": "ContactPoint", "contactType": "customer support", "url": "https://yoursite.com/contact" }

recommendations.recommendation: Add a publication or modified date to your content. 65% of AI crawler hits target content less than 1 year old. Without a parseable date, AI engines may deprioritize your content.
steps: Add a <time> element with a datetime attribute to your page
Add datePublished and dateModified to your JSON-LD schema
Set up a recurring reminder to review content every 6 months
recommendations.codeExample:
<!-- Add/update in your HTML -->
<time datetime="2026-08-29" itemprop="dateModified">2026-08-29</time>

<!-- Add/update in your JSON-LD -->
"dateModified": "2026-08-29"

recommendations.recommendation: Define key terms and concepts clearly (e.g., "X is defined as..." or "X refers to..."). Clear definitions are directly reusable by AI engines.
steps: Identify the 3 to 5 key terms central to your page topic
Add a one-sentence definition for each using the 'X is' or 'X refers to' pattern
Place each definition early in the section that first uses the term
Use a <dl> definition list when the page covers many terms
recommendations.codeExample:
AI SEO is defined as [your one-sentence definition here].

AI SEO
[A clear, concise definition that AI engines can extract and reuse.]
[Second key term]
[The definition of your second most important concept.]

recommendations.recommendation: Start key sentences with direct statements that could serve as standalone answers.
steps: Find paragraphs where the main point is buried after qualifications or context
Move the core assertion to the first sentence of the paragraph
Write opening sentences so they can stand alone as a complete answer
Follow the direct statement with supporting detail, examples, and caveats
recommendations.codeExample:
There are many factors involved, and while it depends on the situation, in most cases companies that invest in AI SEO tend to see better visibility in AI-generated answers.

Companies that invest in AI SEO see better visibility in AI-generated answers. Results depend on content quality, structured data completeness, and how well headings are framed as questions.

recommendations.recommendation: Ensure a balanced density of named entities (2-8 per 100 words). Too few makes content vague; too many makes it hard to parse.
Define technical terms or replace with simpler alternatives. High jargon density reduces AI reusability.
steps: List the 5 most domain-specific terms on the page
For each term: either add a plain-English definition on first use, or replace with simpler language
Use the 'is defined as' or 'also known as' pattern for terms you must keep
Aim for a Flesch Reading Ease score of 60 to 70 by simplifying sentence structure
recommendations.codeExample:
Our RAG-based LLM pipeline leverages semantic chunking and vector embeddings to optimize retrieval latency for enterprise-scale deployments.

Our AI pipeline uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), a technique that combines a language model with a searchable knowledge base, to deliver fast, accurate answers at enterprise scale.

recommendations.recommendation: Add bulleted or numbered lists to organize information. Lists are easily extracted and reused by AI engines.
steps: Identify prose that enumerates 3 or more items in a sentence
Convert those sentences into <ul> or <ol> list elements
Use <ol> for sequential steps and <ul> for unordered collections
Keep list items parallel, each starting with the same grammatical form
recommendations.codeExample:
We offer design, development, and strategy services.

  • Design: UI/UX and brand identity
  • Development: web and mobile engineering
  • Strategy: AI readiness and growth planning
  1. Submit your project brief
  2. Schedule a discovery call
  3. Receive your proposal within 48 hours

recommendations.recommendation: Include relevant statistics and data points to support your content with verifiable claims.
Add Organization structured data or og:site_name to help engines identify the source.
steps: Add an og:site_name meta tag to every page's <head>
Add an Organization JSON-LD block to your site's global <head>
Ensure the organization name is identical across JSON-LD, og:site_name, and visible page content
recommendations.codeExample:
<!-- og:site_name in <head> -->
<meta property="og:site_name" content="Your Organization">

<!-- Organization JSON-LD (add to global site header) -->
<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Organization",
  "name": "Your Organization",
  "url": "https://yoursite.com",
  "logo": "https://yoursite.com/logo.png",
  "sameAs": [
    "https://twitter.com/yourhandle",
    "https://linkedin.com/company/yourcompany"
  ]
}
</script>

recommendations.recommendation: Include publication and last-updated dates using proper HTML5 time elements or schema markup.
steps: Add a visible publication date near the article title or byline
Wrap the date in a <time> element with a machine-readable datetime attribute
Add datePublished and dateModified to your JSON-LD schema
recommendations.codeExample:
Published: 2026-08-29

Updated: 2026-08-29

"datePublished": "2026-08-29", "dateModified": "2026-08-29"

recommendations.recommendation: Include and answer common questions your audience might have. Structure content to directly answer "what is", "how to" style queries.
Add JSON-LD structured data and Open Graph tags to provide machine-readable context.
steps: Add a Article JSON-LD block to your <head> (see code example)
Fill in author, publisher, and date fields with real values
Add og:title, og:description, and og:image <meta> tags
Add a <link rel="canonical"> pointing to the preferred URL
Validate at https://search.google.com/test/rich-results
recommendations.codeExample:
<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Article",
  "headline": "Example Domain",
  "description": "Your page description",
  "author": {
    "@type": "Person",
    "name": "Author Name"
  },
  "publisher": {
    "@type": "Organization",
    "name": "Your Organization"
  },
  "datePublished": "2026-08-29",
  "dateModified": "2026-08-29"
}
</script>

recommendations.recommendation: Add a conclusion section with key takeaways or a summary. This helps AI engines quickly extract the main points.
steps: Add an H2 heading at the end of the page: 'Summary', 'Key Takeaways', or 'Conclusion'
List 3 to 5 bullet points covering the most important points from the page
Keep each bullet to one sentence; conclusion bullets are the most-cited part of a page
Optionally follow the summary with a 'Next Steps' or 'Learn More' section
recommendations.codeExample:
Key Takeaways

  • AI SEO focuses on being cited in generated answers, not ranked in link lists.
  • Structured data, answer capsules, and clear entity attribution are the highest-impact factors.
  • Content freshness acts as a hard gate: AI engines strongly prefer content under 12 months old.

Next Steps

Run an audit on your top pages to identify your highest-priority improvements.

recommendations.recommendation: Align your main topics with your title and headings. Topic consistency helps AI engines understand what your page is about.
Use transition words (however, therefore, additionally) to improve content flow and logical structure.
steps: Add contrast transitions between opposing ideas: 'however', 'although', 'on the other hand'
Add sequence transitions between steps or points: 'first', 'next', 'finally'
Add addition transitions to build on a point: 'additionally', 'furthermore', 'in addition'
Add conclusion transitions at the end of sections: 'therefore', 'as a result', 'in summary'
recommendations.codeExample:
AI engines extract structured content. Many pages have no structure.

Adding headings and lists improves your score.

AI engines extract structured content. However, many pages lack the organization needed for reliable extraction.

Therefore, adding headings and lists directly improves how AI engines process and cite your content.

recommendations.recommendation: Your page has 19 words, which is too thin for AI engines to reference. The ideal range is 300-3000 words.
Found 1 external link. AI engines prefer content with 6+ external references. Add more links to authoritative sources that support your claims.
steps: Identify factual claims that can be supported by an external source
Find authoritative sources: research papers, industry reports, official documentation
Wrap the linked text in a meaningful anchor: describe what you are linking to, not 'click here'
Aim for 6 or more external links per page
recommendations.codeExample:
As referenced in Learn more, [your claim here].

According to [Source Name], [another claim supported by evidence].

recommendations.recommendation: Use a clear H1 > H2 > H3 heading hierarchy. Headings serve as structural anchors that AI engines use to segment and reuse content.
steps: Use exactly 1 H1 tag for the main page title
Use H2 tags for major sections (aim for 3+ sections)
Use H3 tags for subsections within each H2
Never skip levels (e.g., don't jump from H1 to H3)
Frame H2s as questions when possible for answer capsule compatibility

recommendations.recommendation: Your Flesch Reading Ease score is 36 (difficult). A score of 60-70 is ideal for broad AI reusability. Simplify where possible without losing meaning.
Your sections average 17 words. The citation sweet spot is 120-180 words. Consider expanding sections with more detail rather than splitting into many short fragments.
Your average sentence is 6 words. While short sentences are readable, combining some into 12-22 word sentences provides better context for AI summarization.
Break down processes into clear, numbered steps. Step-by-step content is highly reusable by AI engines.
Keep paragraphs between 30-150 words for optimal readability and extractability.
Use bold text, short paragraphs, and frequent headings to improve scannability for both humans and AI.
